To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed scheduling solutions are effective, scalable and robust with respect to the knowledge of the peers’ playout buffers.

the scheduling algorithms proposed in this paper allow to control the trade-off between delay and probability of timely data reception, that the accuracy of the playout buffers’ state information has a limited effect on the performance, and that the solutions scale well with respect to the overlay size.

the probability of timely packet delivery can be improved by using a scheduling algorithm that takes into account the knowledge of the content of the neighbors’ buffers, that this improvement can be further enhanced by increasing the accuracy of this knowledge, and that the improvement is not limited by the overlay size.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of efficient and scalable scheduling algorithms for peer-to-peer streaming.
the tradeoff between the probability of timely delivery and the delay in the mesh-based P2P streaming systems.
how to achieve a trade-off between the probability of timely delivery of a packet at a peer and the delay that a packet is kept in the overlay.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed framework is very effective in evaluating the performance of the proposed solutions.
scheduling at the forwarding peer is a promising approach, and that the proposed framework allows a detailed and accurate evaluation of the performance of scheduling algorithms.

the best solution depends on a number of system parameters, including the number of peers, the playout buffer size and the packet loss rate, and the best solution is the one that minimizes the trade-off between the probability that a packet is played out on time and the average playout delay.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed framework can be used for evaluating the performance of scheduling algorithms and that the framework can be extended to evaluate the effects on the overlay performance due to the dynamicity of the overlay.
the knowledge of the buffer content at the peers’ neighbors can be used to improve the probability of timely packet delivery.
we propose a framework to model mesh-based peer-topeer streaming systems and evaluate four scheduling algorithms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the knowledge of the buffer map is crucial for the performance of the system.
the knowledge of the peers’ playout buffer content is crucial for achieving a good trade-off between delay and playout probability.
the knowledge of the buffer map is not always necessary for good performance and that, under certain conditions, a simple solution can be used instead.
